correctness.rationale: The central symmetral/Wigner relation is reconstructed from paired vertex midpoints and signed-area cancellation, with sign from Brunn–Minkowski. The area of the centrally symmetric equiangular polygon is the explicit pairwise generator sine form. Its circulant eigenvalues are computed by a finite sine sum; the constant eigenvalue vanishes and all nonconstant eigenvalues are positive. Parseval gives the exact deficit, the least eigenvalue gives the parity-dependent best coefficient, and strictly convex central-symmetric polygons with positive soft-mode side lengths attain equality. A separate standard-library checker independently reconstructs 1,163 polygons of orders 2..21, including noncentrally symmetric cases, and soft-mode equality families, with maximum absolute discrepancy below 6e-12. The infinite theorem follows from the symbolic proof; the finite checks alone prove no general case.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The original theorem is recovered by discarding the strictly positive variance term; the reverse implication is invalid without additional quantitative reasoning. The classical FRS Fourier inequality, as quoted in Indrei (2015), bounds n times the sum of squared side lengths minus an area term; rewriting to the squared perimeter introduces the side-length variance with the opposite sign and does not give the exact coefficient without a separate all-frequency minimization. Generic Fourier techniques might make the present calculation derivable, but the exact sharp constant and equality eigenspaces are not stated in the inspected sources. Original FRS full text could not be read; this remains a documented historical-priority risk.

originality.rationale: The antecedent proves only nonnegativity and the zero-deficit characterization; the explicit optimal coefficient by parity and its complete opposite-edge-sum equality eigenspaces are not contained in the inspected statements. The original proof explicitly points to Fourier methods, so only the sharp quantitative constant and classification, not the approach or basic inequality, are claimed as the increment. General polygonal stability literature supplies nonoptimal existence constants, while results on reduced polygons and smooth symmetrizations concern inequivalent invariants. Earlier Fourier material that could contain equivalent algebra remains a stated priority risk, not evidence of coverage.
residual_risks: The 1985 Fisher–Ruoff–Shilleto article was not available in full text. It may contain an equivalent sharp special-case spectral statement despite the later source only citing its method.
The full text of Joós–Lángi (2023) and Indrei–Nurbekyan (2014) was not inspected directly; stronger implicit optimization formulas are possible.
Formula-level novelty is narrower than method-level novelty: discrete Fourier diagonalization is classical and explicitly anticipated in the 2026 motivating paper.
Indexed literature cannot establish universal bibliographic uniqueness.

value.rationale: The motivating Wigner-corrected polygonal isoperimetric theorem had a zero-deficit equality criterion. This result upgrades it, in the natural equality-relevant equiangular subclass, to an exact globally sharp all-order stability theorem measuring imbalance of opposite-edge pairs. The explicit parity split and complete minimizing-mode classification give a quantitative model and identify extremal deformations at every polygon order. They cannot be inferred from qualitative equality alone, and provide a precise geometric cutoff without requiring a broader paper-sized theorem. The result does not assert a new general Fourier technique.
